alternate_names: Gaja Nand Jee Mandir (name in IGNCA documentation)
deities: Lord Ganesha (8-ft tall, 5-ft wide murti said to be swayambhu - self-manifested from rock, per local legend)
festivals: Devuthani Ekadashi (wedding-season first invitations are traditionally offered here, per Hindi press - verify)

history.period: DISPUTED: idol tradition c. 500 years (said to exist since ~1459; News18 Hindi reports the murti manifested from rock 500 years ago); IGNCA documentation dates the structure to the 17th century AD; the brief's 'c. 150 years old' may refer to the present building (verify)
history.summary: Hilltop Ganesha temple in Ratanada, Jodhpur, reached by a flight of steps. Its 8-ft tall, 5-ft wide Ganesha murti is said by locals to be swayambhu, having risen naturally out of the rock - a belief behind its popularity for auspicious occasions, with the first wedding invitation traditionally offered here (per Hindi press). The IGNCA documented it as 'Gaja Nand Jee Mandir' (Serial RJ/JDP-718), dating it to the 17th century AD and noting a Hanuman shrine inside. Travel guides variously claim the temple 'existed since 1459'. AGE CONFLICT: c. 1459 / 17th century / c. 150 years (brief) - unresolved; verify against temple records.

name: Shri Ganesh Temple, Ratanada
town_description: Jodhpur, the Blue City, is the second-largest city of Rajasthan and the historic capital of Marwar - home to Mehrangarh Fort and many old temples, with an airport and major rail junction. Ratanada is a well-known locality in Jodhpur city.

travel.road: About 3 km from Jodhpur bus stand, in the Ratanada locality; regular city buses and autos (per IGNCA).

visitor_information.opening_hours: Morning aarti: 5:30-6:00 AM (summer) / 6:00-6:30 AM (winter); evening aarti: 7:30-8:00 PM (summer) / 7:00-7:30 PM (winter) - per triphobo (verify).
